title: Green Rule (Safety Gate)
concept: The one rule that can't be broken: you have to be able to say the honest thing without being punished for it. If that's not true, everything else stops.
whenToUse: Always — but especially when a topic feels risky to bring up, honesty feels like it'll cost you, or someone starts threatening, shutting down, or getting back at the other.
steps: Say what feels unsafe, in one sentence.
Stop talking about the topic right away — don't try to prove your point first.
Take a Pause + Return, with an exact time to come back.
When you're back, warm up and make sure it's safe again before you return to the topic.
Repair the safety break with a phrase you've both agreed on.

phrases.text: This doesn’t feel safe right now.
Even if I don’t like what you say, I won’t punish you for saying it.

working: A: “I want to be honest, but I’m afraid you’ll shut down. Pause 20 minutes — back at 8:10. I’m trying to stay connected.” B: “See you at 8:10. Not leaving — I’m just overwhelmed.”
notWorking: “Fine, tell me — but if it's what I think, I don't know why we're together.” Now the honest thing gets punished, so next time it won't get said.
activity: Each of you writes one sentence for when something doesn't feel safe. Agree on your default pause length. Practice with one low-stakes but honest example — the listener just acknowledges it, without arguing back.
warn: The Green Rule comes before every other tool in this system.
